title: Slow Cooker Chicken & Noodle Soup
description: A familiar chicken noodle soup that cooks mostly unattended with ordinary freezer and pantry ingredients.

ingredients.item: boneless skinless chicken thighs or breasts

substitutions: Use frozen peas and carrots instead of mixed vegetables.
Use leftover cooked chicken; add it during the final 30 minutes instead of at the beginning.
Use small pasta shells instead of egg noodles.

steps.text: Slow-cook the chicken, broth, and vegetables.
Shred the chicken and cook the noodles at the end.

cookSteps.text: Put 1 1/2 pounds chicken, 4 cups chicken broth, 2 cups water, 2 cups frozen mixed vegetables, and 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning if using into the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6 hours, until the chicken is fully cooked and tender.
Move the chicken to a plate, shred it with two forks, and return it to the slow cooker.
Stir in 3 cups egg noodles. Cover and cook on HIGH for 12–15 minutes, checking near the end, until the noodles are tender.
Taste, season with salt and pepper as needed, and serve hot.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. The noodles soften as they sit; add a splash of broth or water when reheating until steaming hot.

title: Sheet-Pan Lemon Tilapia, Broccoli & Potatoes
description: Thin potato pieces get a head start, then tilapia and broccoli finish on the same pan for an easy fish dinner.

ingredients.item: small potatoes, cut into thin wedges

substitutions: Use frozen broccoli; add it with the fish and expect a little extra moisture.
Use another thin white-fish fillet in place of tilapia.
Use garlic pepper plus a squeeze of lemon if you do not have lemon pepper.

steps.text: Add seasoned tilapia and broccoli and finish together.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a large sheet pan. Toss 1 pound thin potato wedges with 1 tablespoon oil and spread them on the pan.
Toss 4 cups broccoli with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil. Move the potatoes aside and add the broccoli and 4 tilapia fillets to the pan.
Sprinkle the tilapia and vegetables with 1 teaspoon lemon pepper. Drizzle the fish with 1 tablespoon lemon juice if using.
Roast 12–15 minutes more, until the potatoes and broccoli are tender and the fish is opaque and flakes easily.

storage: Refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days. Reheat gently until hot; fish is best reheated only once.

title: Leftover Meatballs & Cheesy Orzo Skillet
description: A few cooked meatballs stretch into a creamy tomato-orzo skillet for a practical leftover dinner.
substitutions: Use cooked sliced sausage instead of meatballs.
Use frozen mixed vegetables instead of peas.
Use Parmesan plus a little extra milk instead of shredded cheese.

steps.text: Simmer orzo with sauce and broth.
Warm the leftover meatballs and finish with cheese.

cookSteps.text: Put 1 cup dry orzo, 1 1/2 cups broth, and 1 cup pasta sauce in a large skillet and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer 8 minutes, stirring twice so the orzo does not stick.
Stir in 8 halved cooked meatballs and 1/2 cup frozen peas. Cover and cook 4–5 minutes, until the orzo is tender and the meatballs are steaming hot.
Remove from the heat, stir in 1/2 cup shredded cheese, and serve.

storage: Use the meatballs within their original safe refrigerated storage window. Refrigerate the finished skillet up to 3 days and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Small-Batch Caramel Apple Crisp
description: One apple becomes a warm two-serving crisp with a simple brown-sugar oat topping and optional caramel drizzle.
equipment: 2 small ramekins or one small baking dish

ingredients.item: apple, peeled or unpeeled and diced

substitutions: Use a ripe pear instead of the apple.
Use quick oats if that is what you have.
Skip the caramel sauce; the brown-sugar topping is sweet on its own.

steps.text: Add oat topping and bake until bubbly.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F. Divide 1 diced apple between 2 small ramekins and toss with 1 teaspoon lemon juice if using.
In a small bowl, mash together 1/4 cup oats, 2 tablespoons flour, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, and 2 tablespoons softened butter until crumbly.
Scatter the topping over the apple. Bake 20–22 minutes, until the apple is tender and the topping is browned.
Cool 5 minutes, then drizzle each serving with up to 1 tablespoon caramel sauce if using.

storage: Refrigerate covered up to 3 days. Reheat gently before serving if desired.
